messages:
lee: Heads-up: linkcheck started failing after the mkdocs -> docusaurus migration on the guides tree. A bunch of anchors that previously worked are 404ing in previews. docsite-bot: CI failure: docs/linkcheck job #201 returned non-zero. Faulty targets: /guides/release-notes#🚀-what-s-new, /sdk/node#client_init, /api/ops#kv-cache ana: Wait, an emoji in the anchor? That seems odd. Which file contains that heading? lee: It's from guides/release-notes.md which includes an external snippet: ``. The snippet starts with: `# 🚀 What's new (release 2.1)` so Docusaurus slugify produces `whats-new-release-21` but mkdocs-linkcheck is resolving a rendered anchor like `-what-s-new` (it keeps the emoji hyphen). That mismatch is the culprit. sam: Can you paste the exact rendered HTML snippet? Sometimes our preprocessor strips emoji differently depending on the include path. lee: Local rendered HTML shows `

🚀 What's new (release 2.1)

` on my machine, while a Docusaurus preview shows `

🚀 What's new (release 2.1)

`. So two different slugifiers in the toolchain. jonathan: This explains other failures too: client_init vs client-initialization and kv-cache vs kv_cache. We have three slug families: dashified, underscored, and emoji-prefixed. sam: Short-term fix: add explicit HTML anchors above the problematic headings in the includes. Example: ` # 🚀 What's new (release 2.1) ` That forces a stable id until we unify slug rules. lee: I pushed a PR that adds explicit anchors and updates internal links to point to the stable ids: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1242. Also normalized SDK anchor names to `client-initialization` and API anchors to `kv-cache`. docsite-bot: PR 1242 triggered preview build. Linkcheck passed on preview (all anchors resolved). ana: Nice. For the long term we should standardize our slugifier across mkdocs and docusaurus or add a transform step that recalculates anchors consistently. sam: Agreed. I created a small script to compare heading -> slug outputs across both generators. Example command to run locally: ``` python tools/slug_check.py docs/guides | rg "emoji|_" -n ``` It prints headings that diverge and suggests canonical ids. jonathan: Filed task DOCS-812 to add the slug-check step into docs CI and to run it on PRs that touch headings or includes. Also added a CONTRIBUTING blurb: avoid using emoji or parentheses in headings used for deep links; prefer explicit anchors for cross-page references. lee: Merged 1242, preview looks good, and I've retriggered the main site deploy. All green now. ana: Thanks team. I'll follow up with a small README in snippets/ explaining the explicit anchor convention so writers know why it's necessary. sam: One more tiny note: when you update anchors, please also run `rg -n "#.*" docs/ | sed -E 's/.*#//' | sort -u` and check for underscores vs dashes. Saves future headaches. lee: Will do. Closing this thread after the deploy completes. :rocket:
